newsitem.title: USA: USDA Fla. orange crop count to pressure prices.
newsitem.headline: USDA Fla. orange crop count to pressure prices.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures prices could fall the limit on the opening on USDA's unchanged estimate of the box count and increase in yields, analysts said.

USDA kept the crop at 220 million 90-lb boxes and raised yields to 1.54 gallons per box from 1.53 gallons. Most market sources had expected USDA would slash both box count and yields after the Jan 19 freeze.
"It's unbelievable," Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said, adding the first estimate was probably too low.
Analysts said prices could open down their 5.00-cent limit in the back months, with spot March down its 10.00-cent limit, and continue to rack up losses for several days.
"We will see new lows, easily, and I wouldn't be surprised to see a "six" as the first digit," Ganes said.
Spot March set a life-of-contact low of 76.40 cents a lb on Jan 13.
Dean Witter vice president Celeste Georgakis said the technical outlook for the market remains negative and the report is likely to induce more follow-through selling.
"Fundamentally, I'm not sure the trade will jump in here and sell the market but overall the report is very bearish," she said.
Furthermore, ample supplies from both Florida and Brazil and sluggish demand, "will not bode too well for the market," Georgakis added.
